rationale: This is a mechanical recombination of two already-tested legs — the identical organic-minus-acquired intangible leg from "Internal Innovation Over Acquisition"/"Cash Surplus Organic Intangibles" and the level-minus-volatility earnings leg already used in "Earnings-Stable Intangible Build" (only the MA window changes from 3 to 5) — so it adds no new economic mechanism.

Both legs are copied verbatim from the archive ("Organic Formation Cash Share" leg 1 and "Internal Innovation Over Acquisition" leg 2), making this a pure cross-pairing of previously evaluated components rather than a substantively different hypothesis.

The reinvestment-mix leg is essentially identical to "Intangible Reinvestment Retention" leg 1 (and a close cousin of "Knowledge Depreciation Mix") while the cash-after-intangibles leg is verbatim from "Cash Surplus Organic Intangibles," so the expected result is a predictable rehash of two already-strong tested legs.

The TS_MIN R&D-floor leg is reused from prior tests, but pairing it with cash-flow-to-current-liabilities introduces a genuinely untested near-term liquidity-coverage dimension (rather than another oancf/at or oancf/sale trend variant), and the construction is clean and sign-coherent, albeit simple and close to a known R&D-intensity × profitability interaction.

The quality leg subtracts dlc/act from MA(oancf/sale) — two ratios with unrelated denominators and very different cross-sectional dispersion — so the leg is not the stated "cash conversion net of short-debt burden" but will be mechanically dominated by whichever component has larger scale, an internally inconsistent construction that a SUMRANK of the two would fix.

The first leg is identical to the archived "Dual-Channel Cash Margin" (same ~3% coverage risk), and the stated motivation is factually wrong — the prior version already used raw xad without COALESCE and in fact delivered fmb 3.01 / ls_talpha 2.51 — so this is a cosmetic quality-leg swap justified by a misdiagnosed failure mode.
